lines.text: Here's a new way for Painful Pleasures' sale pages to take shoppers straight to the deal.
Today, when a shopper clicks a sale item, the product page shows every option, including the ones at full price.
They have to hunt for the discount the card promised.
With the sale-only view, the same click opens the page showing only the options that are on sale and in stock.
A note right above the picker says how many that is.
Whatever they choose stays on a discounted option, and the price shows the markdown.
One click brings back the full range.
When everything is on sale, the page simply says so.
It works on the biggest listings too, like cartridges with a hundred and thirty-six variations, narrowed to the three on sale.
It uses each customer's own pricing, so pro and distributor accounts only see what's actually discounted for them.
It's switched on collection by collection, and we'll A/B test it to measure the lift before rolling it out.
